feedback: Approved to race unchanged. This candidate returns the geometry exactly to iteration 1, the best design so far at 365.78. Iteration 2 showed that moving sensors to y = 0.07 with a 0.04 m spacing (scored 62.76, zero finishes, line_loss_events 2.8 on the oval) is worse, so reverting that is justified. The only controller change is base_speed 1.3 to 1.1, with kp 1.6, kd 0.5, ki 0 and last_direction unchanged. Iteration 1 showed the s-bend ended just past the limit (max_error 0.0613, 19 of 20 off track) and the slalom had max_error 0.063, while speed was the strongest lever in iterations 0 and 1. The oval finished 17 of 20 at a mean of 1.92 s, so there is room under the 3.0 s limit for a slower run. Approving now spends one action run on the race and keeps budget for one revision round if the telemetry shows a clear fix. Read the results as follows. If the s-bend or slalom still show max_error at or above 0.06 m, try base_speed 1.0 next, since speed moved max_error in iterations 0 and 1. If the oval stops finishing or completion_time approaches 3.0 s, go back to base_speed 1.2. If slalom line_loss_events stay above 0.2, test line_loss at search_left or search_right, matching the side the robot leaves the line.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom still end off track with max_error at or above 0.06 m, lower controller.base_speed from 1.1 to 1.0, since iteration 0 to 1 showed speed is the main driver of bend error.
If the oval fails to finish under 3.0 s, raise controller.base_speed to 1.2, since iteration 1 finished the oval at 1.92 s at base_speed 1.3.
If slalom line_loss_events stay above 0.2 (iteration 1 had 0.2), test controller.line_loss at search_left or search_right, matching the side the robot leaves the line.
